main_text.p: testimonio Lactantii, quod in multis brutis et-Lib. 3.c.10.iam[?] loquendi & ridendi vis, aliaque rationis signa deprehendantur.
main_text.head: PROPOSITIO I. Quæ & quanta sit Hominis præstantia.
II. Confutatio argumentorum de ratione brutorum.
De Primo.
main_text.p: De præcellentia Hominis variæ sententiæ: alii eam collocarunt in ratione, alii in risu, alii in sermone, alii in numerandi facultate: alii in erecta corporis figura, &c.
Dic esse præclara & vera hominis elogia, sed non explicare veram ejus Præstantiam.
Opponatur sententia SCRIPTURÆ: Hominem, & quidem solum esse conditum ad Imaginem Dei: ex historia creationis. Hanc esse veram Præstantiam.
Explicetur, & ostendatur: Imaginem Dei non esse corporis formam, cum Deus sit incorporeus: sed consistere 1. in hominis forma essentiali ejusque operationibus: II. in finis præstantia.
Primò, Formam esse ipsam animam: cujus præstantia.I.Forma ho-minis.

1. Insubstantia, quia non ex crasi corporum vel elementorum orta: non harmonia ex compage viscerum & vigore membrorum existens: sicut in fidibus ex intentione nervorum efficiturAristot. lib. 1.de anima

page.notes: The first word of the page, "testimonio", is a continuation from the previous page. The hyphenated word "et-iam" at the line end reads "ct-" in the scan; I read it as "et-" and marked the completed word uncertain. The marginal section sign "I." and the "Lib. 3.c.10." note are partly faint. The page is printed in roman type with small caps in the headings. The printed "II." in the text may be a roman numeral or a sign and is copied as printed.
